title: WHAT IS LEFT MUST BE BURNED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Any meat of the sacrifice left over till the third day must be burned up. If any meat of the fellowship offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not be credited to the one who offered it, for it has become impure; the person who eats any of it will be held responsible.'" - Lev 7:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There is a deadline on this offering. After the third day, it is finished — and eating it then does not merely fail to help. It brings guilt.

Something good had become something harmful, purely through delay.

That is a real spiritual danger. There are things God gives us for a season, and holding on past their time turns blessing into burden. A ministry we should have handed on. A role we should have released. A season of life we should have let close.

There is also the matter of obedience delayed. What God asks of us today is rarely the same thing tomorrow. Felix listened to Paul and said, When I find it convenient, I will send for you (Acts 24:25). That convenient time never came.

Scripture keeps a certain urgency about it: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Heb 3:15). Not because God is impatient, but because delay changes us. The prompting that stirred us on Monday leaves us unmoved by Friday.

Is there something God asked of you that you have been carrying past its day?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an obedience I have delayed until it has gone stale?
2. Am I holding on to something God gave me for a season that has ended?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me the willingness to obey today rather than someday. And give me grace to release what has finished its season. Amen.
